resources.instruction: Before writing the code of each step, confirm: (1) names, directory structure and error handling still match the repository (read the conventions in docs/ and the nearby code); (2) follow the same import, logging and error-wrapping style as the file you are changing; (3) look for an existing helper or utility before creating a new one; (4) extend the existing interface instead of creating a parallel one; (5) check the file list in plan.md so every file is handled. After each changed file, read it again: the code matches the nearby conventions, adds no needless import or dependency cycle, and its signatures and types match the call sites.

Before finishing, check each item yourself: every asynchronous or external call has explicit error handling and does not swallow errors; data from outside is validated at the system boundary; no new TODO or FIXME (if you need a temporary solution, say so clearly in the final answer); the public interface is as small as possible, typed, and matches the spec or contract exactly; only files within the task's scope are changed; new logic has tests for the success path and the main errors; no loose types (`any`, bare casts) without a reason in a comment. Evidence before claims: do not write "passed" or "fixed" if no one ran it; if you could not run a command, say "did not run X" rather than "should pass".
